section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch7 — Learning Theories — Deep 2
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Which of the following is an example of negative reinforcement?

options.option_text: A student completes homework to avoid being kept back during the interval
A student is scolded in front of the class for not doing homework
A student loses ten marks for submitting homework late
A student is praised warmly for neat homework

explanation: Negative reinforcement strengthens a behaviour by removing/avoiding an aversive event. Scolding and losing marks are punishments; praise is positive reinforcement.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch7 — Learning Theories — Deep 2
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A teacher decides to ignore a pupil's attention-seeking calling-out completely. The behaviourist strategy she is applying is:
explanation: Withholding the reinforcer (attention) to weaken a previously reinforced behaviour is extinction.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch7 — Learning Theories — Deep 2
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A child conditioned to fear a white rat also becomes afraid of a white rabbit and cotton wool. This spread of the response to similar stimuli is called:
explanation: Responding similarly to stimuli resembling the conditioned stimulus is generalisation. Discrimination is the opposite — responding only to the specific CS.
